en: Title: *Vajravidāraṇā dhāraṇī* Published: *Āryavajravidāraṇā nāma dhāraṇī*, in: *Dhīḥ* 40 (2005), eds.
Ngawang Samten and Janardan Pandey, pp. 161–164. (not seen)
Input supplied by: Nagarjuna Institute of Exact Methods; standardized.

One of the more influential *dhāraṇīs*, with extensive satellite literature translated into Tibetan (Sakai 1973, cited in Kano 2015). According to the *BEB* on the *Mañjuśrī-vajra-bhairava-tantra* (MVA), pp. 386–387, this work is seen as a precursor to the *Dhyānottarapaṭala* (and consequently to the *Trisamayarāja*, the *Vajrapāṇyabhiṣeka*, and the MVA). (Vvdh_161) Oṃ! Homage to the Blessed Noble Vajravidāraṇā!

Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Vajras. Having empowered his entire body as consisting of vajra, Vajrapāṇi, through the power of the Buddha, entered the vajra-samādhi. Then, through the power of all the Buddhas and by the empowerment of all the Buddhas and all the Bodhisattvas, Vajrapāṇi spoke the Vajrasāra, which has arisen from the Great Wrathful One.

Indestructible, indivisible, true, firm, stable, unimpeded everywhere, undefeated everywhere, causing all beings to flee, causing all beings to be subdued, severing all spells, paralyzing all spells, destroying all ritual actions, causing all ritual actions to flee, subduing all planetary spirits, liberating from all planetary spirits, attracting all spirits, restraining all spirits, bringing to completion all rites of spells and mantras, granting success to those who have not yet succeeded, ensuring the non-destruction of those who have succeeded, bestowing all desires, providing protection for all beings, pacifying, nourishing, paralyzing all beings, and deluding all beings—this mantra of great power, the Lord of Yakṣas Vajrapāṇi proclaimed through the majesty of the Buddha.

Oṃ, homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to Caṇḍavajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas! It is as follows: Oṃ truṭa truṭa, tear apart, tear apart; burst, burst, split open, split open; whirl, whirl, cause to whirl, cause to whirl; awaken, awaken all sentient beings, fully awaken, fully awaken; roam, roam, cause to roam about, cause to roam about; all spirits, crush, crush, completely crush, completely crush; all enemies, strike, strike, strike together, strike together; O Vajra of all vidyās, split with the vajra, split with the vajra; O Vajra, O Vajra, *kaṭa* Vajra, O Vajra, O Vajra, *maṭa* Vajra, O Vajra, O Vajra, *matha* Vajra, O Vajra, O Vajra, to the one who laughs with the *aṭṭahāsa* laugh, the Blue Vajra, the Excellent Vajra, svāhā! Oṃ he fullu nirufullu (? nigṛhṇa kullu mili cullu kuru kullu, for the victory of the Vajra, svāhā! Oṃ, to Kilikīla, svāhā! Oṃ kaṭa kaṭa maṭa maṭa raṭa raṭa, for the crushing and the complete crushing, svāhā! Oṃ cara nicara hara hara sara sara māraya, for the piercing with the Vajra, svāhā! Oṃ chinda chinda bhinda bhinda, to the Great Kilikīla, svāhā! Oṃ bandha bandha krodha krodha, to the Vajra-Kilikīla, svāhā! Oṃ curu curu, to the Fierce Kilikīla, svāhā! Oṃ trāsaya trāsaya, to the Vajra-Kilikīla, svāhā! Oṃ hara hara, to the Holder of the Vajra, svāhā! Oṃ prahara prahara, to the Vajra-Shatterer, svāhā! Oṃ Matisthiravajra, Śrutisthiravajra, Pratisthiravajra, Mahāvajra, Apratihata-vajra, Amoghavajra, Aihivajra, quickly, to the Vajra, svāhā! Oṃ dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru, for the turning back of the entire Vajra family, svāhā! Kill so-and-so, phaṭ!

Oṃ, homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to Caṇḍavajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas! It is as follows: Oṃ hara hara vajra, crush crush vajra, shake shake vajra, burn burn vajra, cook cook vajra, hold hold vajra, maintain maintain vajra, terrible terrible vajra, cut cut vajra, split split vajra, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ, homage to Caṇḍavajrakrodha! Oṃ hulu hulu tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana amṛte hūṃ phaṭ. This is the heart-mantra, the near-heart-mantra, and the root-mantra.
Having brought about the destruction of all evils and the eradication of all suffering,
it is the root of all mantras and is adorned with every splendor.
Having become one whose senses are stilled, [he sees those] whose support is lost and whose life-force is destroyed,
who are encompassed by misfortune and from whom the deities have turned away.
A beloved woman suffers during separation from her husband, and one afflicted by malevolent planets likewise experiences the loss of mutual wealth as well as calamity.
For those afflicted by grief and exhaustion, as well as fear and calamity;
or for those suffering from the afflictions of planets and constellations, or from terrible *kākhorda* spells and malevolent planets;
one sees inauspicious things in dreams, characterized by an abundance of grief and exhaustion.
And this supreme sūtra should be heard by one who is well-bathed and pure;
let those who hear this profound sūtra, which is the domain of the Buddhas, listen.
With serene minds and joyful hearts, adorned with clean garments,
they all [overcome] those wicked-souled ones and the most dreadful calamities.
His vital energy shall be pacified, and he shall attain everything in its entirety;
his lifespan and merit increase, and he is liberated from all sins.
Having filled the golden vessel with water, along with gems, mustard seeds, dūrvā grass, jewels, unbroken rice, sandalwood, and flowers tied with a vajra-knot;
Both the jar and the silver [vessel] should be perfumed with a clean cloth twenty-one times, or likewise one hundred and eight times.
The king who always bathes while reciting the Vidāraṇa mantra,
and who performs this constantly, for him prosperity and auspiciousness are attained.
"Is this correct? Is the primary client the King?
The Blessed One said this, and the monks, that entire assembly, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, garuḍas, and gandharvas, rejoiced and highly praised what the Blessed One had spoken.
The Noble Dhāraṇī named Vajravidāraṇā is completed.
